A_trait: florivory-created calyx hole / legitimate versus robbed access state
decision_note: Primary Iris study compares florivore-protected and unmanipulated plots. Sawfly florivory creates calyx holes and Bombus friseanus shifts from pollinator to robber when holes are available, linking florivory, role switching and reproduction.

A_trait: flower width / nectar accessibility under soil-moisture context
decision_note: Primary Primula florindae study links low soil moisture to narrower flowers and shows the primary bumblebee switches from legitimate visitation to nectar robbing when floral access narrows; robbery experiments quantify male and female fitness consequences.

A_trait: robbed versus unrobbed floral state; nectar reward and flower longevity
decision_note: Primary Salvia castanea study follows nectar robbery, floral visits, pollen deposition and seed set in two populations across 2014-2020. Strong spatiotemporal interaction context, but no independently declared shared plant trait response surface.

Meta-analysis of 153 studies across 120 plant species on floral larceny and reproductive success. Valuable synthesis/source-chasing evidence, but not an independent primary study for the systematic primary-study count.

A_trait: flower number; glucosinolate profile under urbanization context
decision_note: Primary Brassica incana study spans 15 populations along an urbanization gradient and jointly measures pollinator community, herbivory, phenotypic traits and reproductive success. Urbanization reorganizes pollinators and herbivory, but the study does not estimate matched pollinator and antagonist responses to one declared floral trait coordinate.
